literal: Let come indeed the lover one day; I will drink [him] for sorrowful pain all to perish.
translation: If only my lover would return for just one day! I will drink him in, so that all my sorrowful pain perishes.
modern: என் காதலர் ஒருநாள் வருவாராக! என்னுடைய துன்ப நோய் எல்லாம் அழியும்படி நான் அவரைப் பருகுவேன்.
explanation: The speaker expresses a deep, consuming longing for her absent lover's return. She wishes for him to come back for just one day. To cure her lovesickness, she uses the striking metaphor of drinking him in ('பருகுவன்'), as if his presence is a healing draught. This intense visual and physical consumption is meant to completely destroy ('கெட') all her sorrow and pain ('பைதல் நோய்'). The word 'மன்' acts as a particle of intense wishing, emphasizing her desperate yearning.
